claims.text: Higher configurational entropy in the HEA markedly increases lattice distortion.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases dislocation pinning under dynamic loading.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases dislocation interactions under dynamic loading.
The proposed HEA is an as-cast, single-phase FCC material with a uniform microstructure.
Reducing the number of principal elements produces a control alloy with lower configurational entropy.
Lattice distortions in the HEA hinder dislocation motion.
Hindered dislocation motion increases dynamic strain-rate sensitivity.
Hindered dislocation motion increases energy dissipation under dynamic loading.
Dislocations are more strongly interacting and more effectively pinned in the HEA than in the conventional control alloy.
The HEA will have greater dynamic strain-rate sensitivity than the conventional alloy.
The HEA will dissipate more energy than the conventional alloy.
The HEA will exhibit a higher loss modulus than the conventional alloy.
The HEA will exhibit more pronounced damping than the conventional alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase, as-cast FCC HEAs at ambient temperature and moderate dynamic strain rates.
Phase transformations or extreme strain rates or temperatures may alter the microstructure and invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe greater strain-rate sensitivity, energy dissipation, or dislocation-pinning signatures in the HEA relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
